The evaluation points -- the PCS column keys that DECIDE those two numbers -- live in `argument.rs::define`, not in layout.rs.  This script therefore parses `define` as well and derives the group counts from the PCS key rule; layout.rs alone cannot answer R-1.

findings.detail: the measured disclosure of the `one base mask row per claim` control is 15; the tool's helper predicts 14. The helper assumes two singleton groups with the same (rows, row-bit symbols) key leak the SAME functional.  That holds when the row bits are constants (the leak is a row's unit vector) but not when they are symbolic: the surviving base functional is Im(c) Re(a eq) - Re(c) Im(a eq), which depends on the group's own e and lambda, so k singleton groups on one R-row plane span min(k, R) dimensions.  Here SC_QMM / SC_KMM / SC_VMM all open A_Y (rows 12-13) at the same symbolic row bit and recover BOTH rows, and A_X (rows 6-7) is opened by SC_SS and SC_IO_IN.  This script uses the corrected expectation (`native_singleton_expectation`).  It changes no positive verdict: the delivery gives every site a pair, and the control's point (a single base row leaks, the pair closes it) is unaffected.
findings.title: the pair-schedule tool's `singleton_leak_expectation` under-counts this layout's base1 control

findings.detail: layout.rs declares A_GROUPS = 30 and H_GROUPS = 8 as hand counts with no derivation; the PCS column keys that decide them are the evaluation points in argument.rs::define.  Parsing define and applying zkp-core's ZKey rule ((point tail, c0, len), first occurrence) reproduces 30 and 8 exactly, so the two constants the prover and verifier compare the PCS's real grouping against are right.
findings.title: A_GROUPS / H_GROUPS cannot be checked from layout.rs alone

findings.detail: SC_TZC opens A_D, A_DSQ and the nine 32-entry limb sub-planes at ONE point.  Their point tails are identical, so a reader who groups by the tail alone counts one group; the PCS also keys on the column window (c0, len), which splits them into the c0 = 0 group {A_D, A_DSQ, limb 0, limb 8} and seven singletons at c0 = 32..224.  Ignoring (c0, len) would give A_GROUPS = 23 and the prover would refuse its own honest proof with `N opening groups, the schedule declares M`.  The declared 30 is the value the PCS actually produces.
findings.title: the sub-row (c0, len) half of the PCS key carries 7 of the 30 A groups
